notes: Pushbutton straddles the centre gap of the breadboard: the image shows two leg pairs, in columns 10 and 12. Its top legs are in the top half (row e) and its bottom legs in the bottom half (row e). Each top/bottom pair is internally connected when pressed.
The wires start at rows c in the bottom half (columns 10 and 12). Row c is an assumed hole in the same strip as the button's bottom legs (10b, 12b).

The teal wire goes from digital pin 2 to column 10. The black wire goes from the GND pin in the power header (the second GND, GND.2) to column 12. The two wires are on opposite button legs, so pressing the button connects pin 2 to GND.
The image shows the black wire at the power-header GND pin next to VIN, so I used GND.2. GND.1/GND.2/GND.3 are all the same ground net.
Pin 2 uses the internal pull-up (INPUT_PULLUP), so there is no external resistor. Pin 13's onboard LED is part of the Uno, so I did not add it as a part.
The USB cable that connects the Arduino to the computer is not shown in the circuit images. It is not part of the drawn circuit, so I left it out.
